about: Labelled cases for `sf-autopilot audit`, judged against the real Setup Audit Trail of a scratch org on 2026-09-19 (UTC).
The facts are in eval/trail-sf-autopilot-test-2026-09-19.json. Run with scripts/audit-eval.mjs; see docs/audit-command-evaluation.md.
expected is what a careful human auditor, holding only the trail for that window, should answer for a RELEASE GATE:
CONFIRMED only if the trail shows the change was made, to the value named, AND the same trail does not show it undone or replaced afterwards.
So a SUPERSEDED change (fiscal year set to July, then to April) is expected NOT_CONFIRMED: a gate that passes on a step that no longer holds has passed a release on a false premise.

A true NEGATION (nothing of the kind is in the window) is expected CONFIRMED, although the command cannot give that by design: it needs an entry to point at. Those are scored honestly as misses, in their own category.
An OPAQUE entry (reportEscapeCharsPrefOffOn) is expected NOT_CONFIRMED against the plain-English step: nothing in the trail ties the two together.
Labels were fixed before the first run and are not to be changed to match the tool.
windowsNote: A window starts at this instant and runs to now; the runner turns it into --since <minutes>. day = all 61 entries; contacts = from the first contacts toggle (47); trial = from the deliverability changes (27); postdeliv = after them (25); afterjuly = after the fiscal year went 1->7 but before 7->4 (21); late = from the custom field on (12); last = the permanent delete and the password expiry only (2).

cases.prompt: Hi team, following up on the release call from this morning. As discussed with Priya and the platform group, we had a number of manual post-deployment items on the list for this sandbox and I want to be sure the important one is closed out before we sign off on the change record. I know everyone is busy with the regression cycle and the data migration rehearsal, and that the integration team is still waiting on the new named credentials, so I will keep this short even though the background is long. Last quarter we had an incident where emails from the sandbox did not go out to the UAT testers because the deliverability level had been left at the restricted default after a refresh, and nobody noticed for two days, which cost us most of a test cycle and a fairly uncomfortable steering committee meeting. To avoid a repeat, the runbook now says that right after the deployment the email deliverability access level has to be set to All email so that the testers receive their welcome messages and the approval notifications. That is the one thing I need verified here. Everything else on the list, the permission set assignments, the scheduled jobs, the report folders, is covered by the automated checks in the pipeline and does not need a manual look. Thanks a lot for your help on this, and sorry for the long message, I wanted the context to be on record for the auditors.
cases.why: About 1,400 characters of context around one true claim: deliverability set to All email.

cases.prompt: Post-deployment runbook for release 24.9, section 4, manual steps, to be completed by the release engineer on call and countersigned by the platform owner before the change record is closed. Step 4.1: in Setup, under Email, Deliverability, set the access to send email level to All email, so that UAT testers receive notifications. Step 4.2: in Setup, under Company Settings, Company Information, change the default organization time zone to Australia/Brisbane, because the support team works Queensland hours and does not observe daylight saving. Step 4.3: in Setup, under Process Automation Settings, set the default workflow user to Integration User so that time-based workflow runs under the integration account and not under a named person who may leave. Step 4.4: in Setup, under Company Settings, Fiscal Year, set the standard fiscal year to start in October, to match the new group reporting calendar that finance announced last month. Step 4.5: in Setup, under Certificate and Key Management, create a certificate named Autopilot Trial Cert for the identity provider. When every step above is complete, reply on the change record with the time each was done.
cases.why: Five runbook steps, four true; 4.4 says October and the fiscal year was set to April.
